This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. news.titleTr: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board
news.summaryTr: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
news.articleText: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby". The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work. He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area. It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board. An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

news.summary: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.

news.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
news.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
news.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." In a post on social media, Kennedy said: "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles." "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices. - Published24 July - Published30 January - Published24 September

news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. items.articleText: Adil Katılım Bankası'nın faaliyet izni iptal edildi: Temettü dışındaki haklar TMSF'ye devredildi YAYIN TARİHİ, 18 Kasım 2026 02:06 PAYLAŞ - Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurulu, Adil Katılım Bankası A.Ş.'nin temettü dışındaki ortaklık hakları ile yönetim ve denetimini Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'na devretti. Karar 18 Kasım tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurulu (BDDK), Adil Katılım Bankası A.Ş. hakkında karar aldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 18 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan 11601 sayılı Kurul Kararı'na göre bankanın temettü dışındaki ortaklık hakları ile yönetim ve denetimi Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'na (TMSF) devredildi. Karar, BDDK'nın 17 Kasım 2026 tarihli toplantısında yapılan inceleme ve değerlendirmelerin ardından alındı. Karar Bankacılık Kanunu'na dayandırıldı Kurul kararında, Adil Katılım Bankası'nın temettü dışındaki ortaklık hakları ile yönetim ve denetiminin 5411 sayılı Bankacılık Kanunu'nun 71'inci maddesinin birinci fıkrasının (a), (c) ve (d) bentleri kapsamında TMSF'ye devredilmesine hükmedildi. Karar, 18 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanarak duyuruldu.

items.title: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang
items.summary: Nvidia reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday amid the dramatic exit of ex-CEO Jensen Huang.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang
items.summaryTr: Nvidia reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday amid the dramatic exit of ex-CEO Jensen Huang.
items.articleText: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang - Published Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted founder Jensen Huang. In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Collette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this." The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping 5% in after-hours trading. Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a possible spy for China. "The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a Tuesday call with financial analysts. The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period. Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter. Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance. Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worry that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader. "The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment." Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout happening throughout the technology industry. "It is business as usual," she said of what is happening inside of Nvidia now. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us." She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects". "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this." Despite board chairman Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analyst questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement. Jones said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection. "With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new CEO will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."

items.articleText: Türkiye'de yatırım yapan yabancılara 5 yıllık ikamet izni: Alt sınır 150 bin dolar - Türkiye'de yatırım yapacak yabancılara yatırım tutarına göre 3 veya 5 yıl süreli ikamet izni verilecek. En az 150 bin dolar yatırım yapanlar 3 yıl, 200 bin dolar yatırım yapanlar ise 5 yıllık ikamet izni alabilecek. Türkiye'de yatırım yapmayı planlayan yabancılar için yeni ikamet izni düzenlemesi yürürlüğe girdi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın imzasıyla Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan karara göre, belirli yatırım koşullarını karşılayan yabancı yatırımcılara yatırım tutarlarına bağlı olarak 3 veya 5 yıl süreli ikamet izni verilebilecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Düzenleme kapsamında en az 150 bin ABD doları veya karşılığı döviz tutarında yatırım yapan yabancılara 3 yıl süreli ikamet izni düzenlenebilecek. Yatırım tutarının en az 200 bin ABD dolarına veya karşılığı döviz miktarına ulaşması halinde ise ikamet izni süresi 5 yıl olacak. Hangi yatırımlar ikamet izni kapsamında? Kararda, ikamet izni için kabul edilecek yatırım türleri de belirlendi. Buna göre yabancı yatırımcıların aşağıdaki araçlardan biri üzerinden yatırım yapması gerekiyor: - Mevduat: Türkiye'de faaliyet gösteren bankalardaki mevduat hesapları. - Devlet borçlanma araçları: Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığınca ihraç edilen devlet borçlanma araçları. - Gayrimenkul yatırım fonları: Gayrimenkul yatırım fonu katılma payları. - Girişim sermayesi fonları: Girişim sermayesi yatırım fonu katılma payları. - Emeklilik planları: Sigortacılık ve Özel Emeklilik Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu tarafından belirlenen emeklilik planlarına dahil olma. Yatırımın uygunluğu, tercih edilen yatırım aracına göre ilgili banka veya kamu kurumu tarafından tespit edilecek. Yatırımın en az yarısı kadar süre korunması gerekecek Düzenlemede dikkat çeken şartlardan biri de yatırımın korunma süresi oldu. Yabancı yatırımcıların gerçekleştirdikleri yatırımları, aldıkları ikamet izninin toplam süresinin en az yarısı boyunca muhafaza etmesi gerekecek. Buna göre 3 yıllık ikamet izni alanların yatırımlarını en az 1,5 yıl, 5 yıllık ikamet izni alanların ise en az 2,5 yıl boyunca koruması gerekecek. Bu koşulun sağlanıp sağlanmadığı, yatırımın türüne göre yetkili banka veya ilgili düzenleyici kurum tarafından kontrol edilecek. Başvuru şartlarını İçişleri Bakanlığı belirleyecek Yeni uygulama kapsamında yabancı yatırımcılara sunulacak hizmetler ve başvuru işlemlerine ilişkin usul ve esaslar İçişleri Bakanlığı tarafından belirlenecek. Karar kapsamında düzenlenecek ikamet izinleri, Türk Vatandaşlığı Kanunu'nun 12'nci maddesi çerçevesinde değerlendirilmeyecek. Dolayısıyla bu düzenleme doğrudan vatandaşlık hakkı sağlamıyor. Cumhurbaşkanı Kararı, 18 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanarak yürürlüğe girdi.

items.articleText: 7 ülkeden iplik ithalatına 5 yıl daha damping vergisi: Oranlar belli oldu - Çin, Hindistan, Endonezya ve 4 ülkeden sentetik iplik ithalatına uygulanan dampinge karşı önlemler 5 yıl daha devam edecek. Ticaret Bakanlığı, ülke ve firmalara göre değişen vergi oranlarını açıkladı. Ticaret Bakanlığı, Çin, Endonezya, Hindistan, Malezya, Pakistan, Tayland ve Vietnam menşeli sentetik veya suni devamsız liflerden ipliklerin ithalatına yönelik dampinge karşı önlemlerin devam etmesine karar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 18 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan 2026/32 sayılı Tebliğ ile söz konusu ülkelerden yapılan kesik elyaf ipliği ithalatına uygulanan mevcut önlemler 5 yıl daha yürürlükte kalacak. Karar, Bakanlığın yürüttüğü nihai gözden geçirme soruşturmasının tamamlanmasının ardından alındı. Soruşturma sonucunda, önlemlerin kaldırılması halinde damping ve yerli üretim sektöründe oluşan zararın devam etmesinin veya yeniden ortaya çıkmasının muhtemel olduğu tespit edildi. Vergiler ülkeye ve firmaya göre değişiyor Dampinge karşı önlemler, ürünün menşe ülkesi ve üretici firmaya göre farklı oranlarda uygulanacak. Bazı ülkelerde kilogram başına dolar tutarı, bazılarında ise CIF bedeli üzerinden yüzde olarak hesaplama yapılacak. Tebliğde öne çıkan oranlar şöyle: Malezya'da Penfabric için yüzde 17,03, Recron için yüzde 11,26; Pakistan'da Din Textile Mills için yüzde 10,02, Margalla ve Monnoowal Textile Mills için yüzde 6,62 oranları belirlendi. Tayland'da Indo-Thai Synthetic için yüzde 7,79, Lucky Spinning için yüzde 14,02 oranında önlem uygulanacak. Vietnam'da ise firma bazında yüzde 19,48 ile yüzde 23,91 arasında değişen oranlar yer alıyor. İthalatta 5 yıllık yeni dönem başladı Tebliğ kapsamında belirlenen dampinge karşı önlemler, yayımlandığı 18 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yürürlüğe girdi. Gümrük idareleri, kapsamdaki ürünlerin serbest dolaşıma giriş rejimi çerçevesindeki ithalatında belirlenen tutar ve oranlarda kesin önlem tahsil edecek. Düzenlemeye göre önlemler, yürürlük tarihinden itibaren 5 yıl sonra sona erecek. Ancak süre dolmadan yeni bir nihai gözden geçirme soruşturması başlatılması halinde önlemler, soruşturma tamamlanana kadar uygulanmaya devam edecek. Karar, sentetik ve suni devamsız liflerden iplik ithalatında mevcut ticaret önlemlerinin korunmasını sağlayacak.

items.title: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
items.summary: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
items.summaryTr: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
items.articleText: Article: published on 17 November 2026 American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody - Published A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said. The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police. Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. Counter Terrorism Policing said he is now in US custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said it had "nothing to do with it". British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service. The day after Tyner's arrest on 10 November, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to. "We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow. On Tuesday, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress." "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added. Tyner's arrest was the result of a long-running operation by MI5 - the UK's domestic intelligence and security agency - in collaboration with the FBI, the BBC understands. He had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq, but at the time of his arrest was working with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester - where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information which would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia. Detectives sent the Crown Prosecution Service a file on the senior US soldier's alleged spying for consideration - allegations described by the head of Counter Terrorism Policing as "extremely serious." But at that stage the Attorney General's Office in London got involved. As did the US authorities. And now the decision has been taken that Lieutenant Colonel Tyner should be taken into custody by the US Military. It means he will not stand trial in the UK, but under US Uniform Code of Military Justice. FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners. "Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk." US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take. "Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added. items.titleTr: Thomas Markle charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines
items.summaryTr: Markle is being held in prison in the US on a separate charge and has previously denied all of the allegations.
items.articleText: Thomas Markle charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines - Published Police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material. The charges were filed on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC. Earlier this month, the 82-year-old was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents, after searching storage units Markle rented, seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books, that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Markle, who is in custody, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney in the US for comment. Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had charged Markle Sr with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material". Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country. Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr. Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor. Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. items.articleText: Huang'ın ayrılığı sonrası kriz büyüyor: SEC, Nvidia'ya soruşturma başlattı - ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu'nun (SEC), yatırımcıların yanıltılıp yanıltılmadığını belirlemek amacıyla Nvidia hakkında sivil soruşturma başlattığı öne sürüldü. İddia, Jensen Huang'ın CEO'luktan ayrılmasının ardından şirket üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. ABD'li çip üreticisi Nvidia, CEO Jensen Huang'ın ayrılığının ardından yeni bir soruşturma iddiasıyla gündeme geldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle The Wall Street Journal'ın haberine göre ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu (SEC), şirketin yatırımcılara yaptığı açıklamaların yanıltıcı olup olmadığını incelemek üzere sivil soruşturma başlatıyor. Söz konusu iddia, Nvidia'nın yönetim değişikliği ve Çin'e çip ihracatı tartışmalarıyla gündemde olduğu bir dönemde geldi. Çin'e çip sevkiyatı ve Megaspeed bağlantısı mercek altında Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang, evlilik dışı ilişkilerine ilişkin haberlerin ardından görevinden ayrılmıştı. İddialar arasında, Singapur merkezli veri şirketi Megaspeed'in yöneticisi Alice Huang ile ilişkisi de yer alıyordu. ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı'nın, 2024'ün sonlarından bu yana Megaspeed hakkında soruşturma yürüttüğü belirtiliyor. Şirketin Nvidia çiplerinin bir bölümünü Çin'e yönlendirmiş olabileceği şüphesi araştırılıyor. Böyle bir sevkiyatın ABD ihracat yasalarını ihlal edebileceği ifade ediliyor. ABD Kongresi de Jensen Huang'ın söz konusu ilişki ve bunun Çin'e yönelik çip ihracatı kısıtlamalarının gevşetilmesi yönündeki tutumuna olası etkileri hakkında soruları yanıtlamasını talep etmişti. ABD Hazine Bakanı'ndan Nvidia'ya ağır suçlama ABD Hazine Bakanı Scott Bessent de hafta sonunda Nvidia'ya yönelik sert açıklamalarda bulundu. Bessent, şirketin gelirlerini ve kârını artırmak amacıyla güçlü çipleri Çin'e bilerek sattığını öne sürdü. Bu açıklamalar, Washington yönetiminin Nvidia'nın Çin'e yönelik çip satışlarına ilişkin denetim ve ihracat kısıtlamalarını artırdığı bir dönemde geldi. Nvidia'nın geliri yüzde 103 arttı SEC soruşturması iddiası, Nvidia'nın finansal sonuçlarını açıkladığı gün gündeme geldi. Şirket, mali yılının üçüncü çeyreğinde 115,8 milyar dolar gelir elde etti. Bu rakam, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 103 artışa işaret etti. Buna karşın Nvidia hisseleri, Huang'ın CEO'luk görevinden ayrılmasından bu yana yüzde 10'dan fazla değer kaybetti. Yatırımcılar, şirketin güçlü gelir büyümesinin yanı sıra yönetim değişikliği, Çin'e çip ihracatı ve ABD'deki düzenleyici incelemelerin Nvidia'nın geleceğine etkisini takip ediyor.

items.articleText: İsrail Meclisi'nde Netanyahu'nun adayı kaybetti: Başkanlık koltuğuna muhalefet geçti - İsrail Meclisi'nde yapılan başkanlık seçiminde muhalefetin adayı Matan Kahana 66 oy alırken, Netanyahu liderliğindeki koalisyonun adayı Ofir Katz 52 oyda kaldı. Arap partilerinin desteğiyle kazanılan sonuç, muhalefet blokunun 67 sandalyelik çoğunluğunu ortaya koydu. İsrail Meclisi'nde (Knesset) yeni başkanı belirlemek için yapılan oylamada, muhalefet blokunun ortak adayı Yashar Partisi Milletvekili Matan Kahana seçildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 120 sandalyeli Meclis'te yapılan oylamada Kahana 66 milletvekilinin desteğini alırken, geçici Başbakan Binyamin Netanyahu liderliğindeki koalisyonun adayı Likud Milletvekili Ofir Katz 52 oyda kaldı. İki milletvekili ise oy kullanmadı. Gadi Eisenkot liderliğindeki muhalefet blokunun adayı Kahana, Arap partilerinin desteğiyle Meclis Başkanlığı koltuğuna oturdu. Arap partilerinin 19 sandalyesi belirleyici oldu İsrail'de 27 Ekim'de yapılan seçimlerin ardından Meclis'teki sandalye dağılımı, başkanlık oylamasında belirleyici oldu. Netanyahu liderliğindeki blok 53 sandalye kazanırken, Yahudi muhalefet partileri 48, Arap partileri ise 19 sandalyeye ulaştı. Eisenkot liderliğindeki muhalefet bloku ile Arap partilerinin toplam sandalye sayısı 67'ye yükseldi. Bu destek, Kahana'nın Meclis Başkanı seçilmesini sağladı. Muhalefet yargı reformu yasalarını gündeme taşıyacak Kahana'nın Meclis Başkanı seçilmesinin ardından muhalefet blokunun, Netanyahu hükümetinin geçirdiği tartışmalı yargı reformu düzenlemeleri ve diğer bazı yasaların iptaline yönelik yasa tekliflerini sunması bekleniyor. Meclis Başkanlığı değişimi, muhalefetin yasama gündeminde daha fazla söz sahibi olmasının da önünü açıyor. İsrail'de hükümet kurulabilmesi için 120 üyeli Meclis'te en az 61 milletvekilinin güvenoyunu alması gerekiyor. items.title: CEO'su gitti, Nvidia'nın büyüme iştahı bitmedi: Bilançodan Wall Street'e ters köşe
items.summary: Jensen Huang'ın CEO'luk görevinden ayrılmasının ardından ilk finansal tahminini açıklayan Nvidia, dördüncü çeyrek gelirinin 130 milyar dolara ulaşmasını bekliyor. Şirketin tahmini, Wall Street beklentilerini geride bıraktı.

items.titleTr: CEO'su gitti, Nvidia'nın büyüme iştahı bitmedi: Bilançodan Wall Street'e ters köşe
items.summaryTr: Jensen Huang'ın CEO'luk görevinden ayrılmasının ardından ilk finansal tahminini açıklayan Nvidia, dördüncü çeyrek gelirinin 130 milyar dolara ulaşmasını bekliyor. Şirketin tahmini, Wall Street beklentilerini geride bıraktı.
items.articleText: CEO'su gitti, Nvidia'nın büyüme iştahı bitmedi: Bilançodan Wall Street'e ters köşe - Jensen Huang'ın CEO'luk görevinden ayrılmasının ardından ilk finansal tahminini açıklayan Nvidia, dördüncü çeyrek gelirinin 130 milyar dolara ulaşmasını bekliyor. Şirketin tahmini, Wall Street beklentilerini geride bıraktı. Dünyanın en değerli çip üreticilerinden Nvidia, uzun yıllardır şirketin başında bulunan Jensen Huang'ın ayrılığının ardından açıkladığı ilk finansal tahmininde piyasa beklentilerini aştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, mali yılın dördüncü çeyreğinde gelirinin 130 milyar dolar, artı veya eksi yüzde 3 seviyesinde gerçekleşmesini beklediğini duyurdu. LSEG tarafından derlenen verilere göre analistlerin ortalama gelir beklentisi 125,25 milyar dolardı. Nvidia hisseleri, açıklamanın ardından seans sonrası işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 2 yükseldi. Şirketin hisseleri salı günkü normal seansı ise yıl başından bu yana yaklaşık yüzde 17 düşüşle tamamlamıştı. Nvidia, açıkladığı gelir tahmininde Çin'e yönelik veri merkezi çipi satışlarından herhangi bir katkı varsaymadığını da belirtti. Huang'ın ayrılığı şirketin geleceğine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırdı Jensen Huang'ın ayrılığı, Nvidia'nın yönetim yapısının yanı sıra şirketin yapay zeka ekosistemindeki rolüne ilişkin belirsizlikleri de artırdı. Yatırımcılar, Nvidia'nın bulut hizmeti sağlayıcılarına, tedarikçilerine ve yapay zeka girişimlerine yaptığı milyarlarca dolarlık yatırımların geleceğini ve şirketin yeni CEO'sunun kim olacağını yakından takip ediyor. Reuters'ın aktardığına göre Huang, evlilik dışı ilişkilerine ilişkin ortaya çıkan haberlerin ardından perşembe günü görevinden ayrıldı. Bu ilişkiler arasında Çinli iş insanı Alice Huang ve iki Nvidia çalışanının da bulunduğu belirtildi. ABD istihbarat kurumlarının, Alice Huang'ın Çin Devlet Güvenlik Bakanlığı ile bağlantılarının kapsamını ve Pekin'e herhangi bir bilgi aktarıp aktarmadığını araştırdığı bildirildi. Bu bilgiler, konuya yakın iki kaynağa dayandırıldı. Huang'ın ayrılması, Nvidia'nın çip yol haritası, müşteri anlaşmaları ve Washington ile ilişkilerinde yaklaşık 30 yıllık kurucu liderlik dönemini sona erdirdi. Yeni CEO arayışı sürüyor Nvidia Finans Direktörü Colette Kress, yeni CEO belirlenene kadar geçici CEO olarak görev yapıyor. Yönetim kurulu, şirketin yeni lideri için hem şirket içinden hem de dışarıdan adayları değerlendiriyor. Şirket içinde Huang'ın geri dönmesini isteyen bir kampanya da yürütülüyor. Ancak Reuters'a konuşan üç kaynak, yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın görevine geri dönmesini değerlendirmediğini aktardı. Huang ise salı günü yaptığı açıklamada, yönetim kurulunun dönüşünün hissedarlar, çalışanlar ve şirket açısından en doğru karar olduğuna kanaat getirmesi halinde CEO olarak geri dönmekten onur duyacağını söyledi. Yönetim kurulu, Huang'ın ayrılığından sonraki ilk önemli yönetişim adımı olarak ulusal güvenlik ve ihracat kontrollerine ilişkin bir komite de oluşturdu. ABD'nin çip ihracatı politikası Nvidia'yı yakından ilgilendiriyor Washington yönetimi, Güneydoğu Asya'ya ve Çinli şirketlere hizmet veren yurt dışındaki veri merkezlerine yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında lisans kurallarını sıkılaştırdı. ABD'li milletvekilleri, Çin'e daha fazla çip ihracatını savunan Huang'ı da sorgulamaya hazırlanıyor. Yatırımcıların bir diğer endişesi ise Nvidia'nın müşterilerine finansman sağlamaya devam edip etmeyeceği. Şirketin bu uygulaması, bazı eleştirmenler tarafından döngüsel finansman olarak nitelendiriliyor. Yeni nesil Vera Rubin çipleri mercek altında Açıklanan finansal sonuçlar, Nvidia'nın Grace Blackwell serisinin halefi olan yeni nesil yapay zeka işlemcisi Vera Rubin'e ilişkin ilk değerlendirmelerden birini de sunuyor. Nvidia, ağustos ayında Vera Rubin'in ekim çeyreğinde veri merkezi gelirlerinin yaklaşık beşte birini oluşturacağını açıklamıştı. Şirket aynı dönemde gelecek mali yılda gelirlerinde yüzde 70 büyüme öngörmüştü. Yatırımcılar, CEO değişiminin ardından şirketin yapay zeka yatırımlarındaki büyümeyi ve pazar liderliğini nasıl sürdüreceğine ilişkin işaretleri takip ediyor.

items.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
items.summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.

items.titleTr: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
items.summaryTr: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
items.articleText: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before". Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014. The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018. In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands. "We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC. He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians". Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got." The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage". The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed. Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch. The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies. On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge. Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. items.titleTr: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board
items.summaryTr: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
items.articleText: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board - Published A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media. The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement. The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way. Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police. Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby". The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work. He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby. CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen. The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area. It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board. An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

items.titleTr: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
items.summaryTr: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
items.articleText: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - Published After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections. The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year. "These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination." He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission. Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates. US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years. Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections. Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status". "Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans. "Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities." In a post on social media, Kennedy said: "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles." "We are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment." The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards". The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths. But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems. The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns. An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials. Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database. Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics. The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge. President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine. Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates. "It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top." The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices. - Published24 July - Published30 January - Published24 September

items.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9327-26 CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today released the agenda for an industry roundtable to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9318-26]. Among other topics, attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization, margin, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. “From the outset of my chairmanship, I have been clear the CFTC will promote innovation in our derivatives markets in a manner attentive to the nuances of these markets and the varied asset classes that underpin them,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I look forward to hearing directly from industry stakeholders on the ways 24/7 trading would impact their respective business models to ensure the Commission is appropriately tailoring its regulatory regime for all market participants.” View the full agenda here. This meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Dial-in information appears below. For the highest quality, select the number nearest your current location. - New York: 646-828-7666 - New Jersey: 551-285-1373 - San Jose: 669-254-5252 or 669-216-1590 - US toll free: 833-568-8864 or 833-435-1820 - US Spanish-language line: 646-964-1167 or 415-449-4000 - International Numbers - Webinar ID: 165 708 9557 - Passcode: 669856 Individuals with additional questions should contact [email protected]. The views, opinions, and information expressed by roundtable participants are solely those of the respective participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government. -CFTC-
